title: Simple-root distributions and infinitesimal subalgebra calculus
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B$ with unipotent radical $U$, projection $\pi_T:B\to T$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, and coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; a Borel is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup; the unipotent radical is the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Choose root parametrizations $x_i:\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{\alpha_i}$ for $\alpha_i\in\Delta$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Put $\epsilon:F[U]\to F$, evaluation at the identity, and $\mathfrak m=\ker\epsilon$. Define the distribution algebra $H=\operatorname{Dist}(U)=\bigcup_{r\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_F(F[U]/\mathfrak m^{r+1},F)$, with product $(ab)(f)=(a\otimes b)(\Delta_U f)$, where $\Delta_U$ is induced by multiplication in $U$. Its unit is $\epsilon$. Let $D_i^{(n)}\in H$ be $f\mapsto[t^n]x_i^*f$ for $n\geq0$. A rational module means a vector space with a coassociative counital coordinate-algebra coaction $c$; a distribution $a$ acts by $(1\otimes a)c$. Let $\mathfrak u=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ be the subspace of $H$ consisting of $F$-linear maps $y:F[U]\to F$ with $y(fg)=\epsilon(f)y(g)+y(f)\epsilon(g)$, and let $A\subseteq H$ be the unital subalgebra generated by this subspace. Then $H$ is generated as a unital $F$-algebra by all $D_i^{(n)}$, for $i\in\Delta$ and $n\geq0$. Write $e_i=D_i^{(1)}\in\mathfrak u$. For $0\leq b<p$ one has
$$D_i^{(b)}=e_i^b/b!\in A.$$
Conjugation by $x_i(t)$ preserves $A$ as a rational action. More explicitly, for $a\in A$ write its finite expansion under conjugation as
$$\operatorname{Ad}(x_i(t))(a)=\sum_{r\geq0}C_{i,r}(a)t^r.$$
Every coefficient $C_{i,r}(a)$ lies in $A$, and for every $n\geq0$ one has in $H$
$$D_i^{(n)}a=\sum_{r+b=n}C_{i,r}(a)D_i^{(b)}.$$
Conjugation here is the action on distributions induced by the group-scheme map $u\mapsto x_i(t)u x_i(-t)$; the coefficient formula is an equality of distributions and hence holds on every rational $U$-module. When $\Delta$ is empty, $U=1$ and $H=A=F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-borel-kostant-distribution-comparison] to the given simply connected semisimple $S$ and the prescribed simple root parametrizations. Obtain $\mathfrak g$, all positive $x_\beta$ and $\Psi$ with the displayed generator values. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], for any enumeration $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_N$ of $\Phi^+$ the map $(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\mapsto x_{\beta_1}(t_1)\cdots x_{\beta_N}(t_N)$ identifies $F[U]$ with $F[t_1,\ldots,t_N]$ and $\mathfrak m$ with $(t_1,\ldots,t_N)$. Write $D_\beta^{(m)}(f)=[t^m]x_\beta^*f$. Iterating the definition of convolution shows that $D_{\beta_1}^{(a_1)}\cdots D_{\beta_N}^{(a_N)}$ is the coefficient functional $[t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_N^{a_N}]$ in these coordinates. The functionals with $\sum a_j\leq d$ are the dual basis of $F[U]/\mathfrak m^{d+1}$. Thus all the ordered products span $H$. Each lies in the image of $\Psi$, by its generator values and multiplicativity, so $\Psi$ is surjective.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-positive-kostant-simple-divided-generation] for the rational Chevalley basis just obtained. It says that $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$ is generated over $\mathbf Z$ by the simple positive divided powers. After tensoring with $F$, every element is therefore an $F$-linear combination of words in $1\otimes e_i^{(m)}$. Their images under $\Psi$ are exactly the given $D_i^{(m)}$. Surjectivity from step 1 proves that these generate $H$. The integral generation is used before reduction, so this argument never divides by a bad-prime root-string constant.

proof.text: For a fixed simple $i$, the group homomorphism $x_i$ gives $x_i(s)x_i(t)=x_i(s+t)$. Applying the definition of convolution and taking the coefficient of $s^a t^b$ yields $D_i^{(a)}D_i^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}D_i^{(a+b)}$. In particular $D_i^{(0)}=\epsilon$ and induction gives $e_i^b=b!D_i^{(b)}$. Also $e_i(fg)=\epsilon(f)e_i(g)+e_i(f)\epsilon(g)$ by the coefficient of $t$ in $x_i^*(fg)$, so $e_i\in\mathfrak u$. For $b<p$, every factor of $b!$ is nonzero in $F$, and therefore $D_i^{(b)}=e_i^b/b!\in A$, including $b=0$.

proof.text: Conjugation fixes the identity, hence preserves every power of $\mathfrak m$. The polynomial coordinates in step 1 make $F[U]/\mathfrak m^{d+1}$ finite dimensional. Pullback by $(t,v)\mapsto x_i(t)v x_i(-t)$ therefore gives a polynomial family of linear operators on this quotient, and its dual gives a finite expansion for every order-at-most-$d$ distribution. It respects convolution because conjugation is a group automorphism, and satisfies the action law by $x_i(s+t)=x_i(s)x_i(t)$. For $y\in\mathfrak u$, its conjugate obeys the augmentation derivation identity over $F[t]$: conjugation preserves both products and $\epsilon$. Comparing coefficients of $t$ shows that every coefficient again lies in $\mathfrak u$. Every $a\in A$ is a finite linear combination of finite products of such $y$ and the unit. Expand the conjugate of each product as a product of its finite coefficient expansions; each resulting coefficient is a product of elements of $\mathfrak u$ and hence belongs to $A$. This proves rationality, finiteness and $C_{i,r}(a)\in A$ for every $r$, without assuming that $A=H$.

source.place: Section 1, printed pp.150--151, and proof of Lemma 2.3, printed p.155; online source as in the node source. Coefficient and finite-jet details supplied by the agent.

proof.text:
Fix $a\in A$ and $f\in F[U]$. Write $a_v$ for applying $a$ in the variable $v$. The polynomial group identity $x_i(t)v=(x_i(t)v x_i(-t))x_i(t)$ gives
$$a_v f(x_i(t)v)=(\operatorname{Ad}(x_i(t))a)_w f(w x_i(t)).$$
The coefficient of $t^n$ on the left is $(D_i^{(n)}a)(f)$ by convolution. On the right substitute the finite expansion from step 4. The coefficient of $t^n$ is $\sum_{r+b=n}(C_{i,r}(a)D_i^{(b)})(f)$, again by convolution. Equality for every $f$ is the asserted equality in $H$. For a rational module with coaction $c$, coassociativity gives $(ab)v=a(bv)$ directly by applying $1\otimes a\otimes b$ to the iterated coaction, so the same equality holds on every such module, with no finite-dimensionality requirement. When $\Delta=\varnothing$, the positive root system is empty, and [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] gives $U=1$. Then $F[U]=F$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $H=F$, $\mathfrak u=0$ and $A=F$.

Mathieu is not stored locally, so I checked against Milne iAG §10l (Dist definition, pp.207-208) and §23h (153)/Thm 23.72-23.74 (Chevalley Z-models, pp.509-511). Step 1: root-product-coordinates applies because semisimple implies reductive (borel-pair node), with any enumeration and any x_beta. Iterated convolution of ordered divided powers is the monomial coefficient functional, and these span each jet dual, so Psi is onto; the step uses only the stated content of the comparison node. Step 2: integral simple generation is tensored over Z before reduction, so no bad-prime constant is inverted. Steps 3-5 are elementary and I checked them: the binomial law from x(s)x(t)=x(s+t); phi^*(m^{d+1}) is in F[t] tensor m^{d+1}, so conjugation has finite expansions and preserves u and A; x(t)v=(x(t)vx(-t))x(t) gives sum C_r(a)D^(b) in the stated order and convention; coassociativity transfers it to rational modules; empty Delta gives U=1. New node positive-kostant-simple-divided-generation is true (q=1 Lusztig; tested on A2, rank 1, R empty) and does not duplicate kostant-integral-pbw (all roots) or the straightening nodes. New node borel-kostant-distribution-comparison is true (isomorphism theorem and the Chevalley Z-model) and asserts no surjectivity or generation, so it is not a restatement; no isomorphism theorem or Dist comparison exists in the DAG.
